_note: This project's own documentation governance. It is deliberately separate from the workspace policy above it: a nested git repository's files are invisible to the outer repository's `git ls-files`, and this checker scans exactly that, so one policy cannot span both trees. Enforcement is local -- a pre-commit hook that is not tracked, and so is absent from any clone.

permitted.reason: the catalogue index and any documentation that describes the solution as a whole rather than one pattern

each pattern's own documentation and supporting learning material, kept with the pattern so the folder is self-contained. Graded by tools/pattern_docs_check.py, which applies the same naming, frontmatter and version rules used under docs/ -- mdgs_check.py cannot, because it grades paths anchored at the repository's own docs/ folder and nothing else
inherited from the governance baseline, which a repository policy may add to but never narrow. This project contains no such folder and adds none
inherited from the governance baseline. Reserved for community health files if this project is ever published

permitted_basenames.name: README.md
permitted_basenames.reason: each pattern documents itself in the folder holding its code, so a reader studying that folder never has to leave it to learn what is being demonstrated. This is stated as a basename rule rather than a permitted folder because the path registry is folder-scoped and pattern documentation deliberately has no folder of its own -- it sits beside the code. It also serves its conventional purpose as a folder index at any depth

placement._note: Placement decides where a document type lives in the central docs/ tree. It does not apply to patterns/*/docs/, where the pattern folder is the placement: a document there belongs to the pattern that owns the folder, and moving it by type would defeat the reason it is there.
